shortDescription: Nordic forward power prices rose on Monday, with both the front-quarter and the front-year contracts scaling multi-year peaks, supported by gains in European energy markets and forecasts for dry weather over the coming weeks.

children: Nordic forward power prices rose on Monday, with both the front-quarter and the front-year contracts scaling multi-year peaks, supported by gains in European energy markets and forecasts for dry weather over the coming weeks.
The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) rose €5.65, or 5.1%, to €117.4 per megawatt-hour (MWh) at 1030 GMT, its highest level since December 2022.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) gained €2.70, or 4%, to €70.45 per MWh, its highest level since July 2023.
"Both rising gas prices and a drier weather outlook are supporting today's rise," said LSEG power analyst Ole Djupskaas.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices rose to their highest intraday levels since late 2022, as diplomatic efforts to open the Strait of Hormuz faltered at a time when Europe is heading into winter with decades-low storage.

The German year-ahead power contract reached another multi-year high, with prices at levels not seen since October 2023, as new strikes in the Middle East compounded supply concerns and drove up fuel prices.
Germany's year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, rose €3.52, or 2.65%, to €136.32 per MWh.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) fell to 11.46 terawatt-hours (TWh) below normal on Monday from 8.67 TWh below normal on Friday.

On the weather front, "the new runs show a slightly stronger trend towards high pressure over the continent extending into the northern parts of Europe and especially the week after next week could see a drier trend in Scandinavia," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
Dry weather forecasts and lower hydro reserves support Nordic power prices as they tighten hydroelectric supply.
